items.title: Arthur Vigne Interview, 1961-11-29
items.q: I remember King Oliver well, he was a big, heavy set dog fella, had a cataract on one eye.

ctx.x: Any other impressions, Russell? No. I should have mentioned on this tape in the beginning that Russell Levy is here also helping with the interviewer, this is Bill Russell, so we identify our voices on the tape in case the secretary later will be listening to this, to some of it to write down some of it. Is there anything else you'd like to add about either your life or the old times of dancing, anything else you can remember about your father or any of the other old time musicians? You did mention, I believe…

Yeah, he worked with King Oliver. King Oliver worked with my daddy and worked with my brother. I remember King Oliver well, he was a big, heavy set dog fella, had a cataract on one eye. I remember him well, he was by my house right now, I remember him. I remember King Oliver well. And I remember Lewis Armstrong when he used to play in the yards uptown when he first started out. Now they had a picture of him when he was a boy in short pants in, what's this fella? Red, oh I can't remember, they had a place up here…
With a trumpet or just standing there?

items.title: Arthur Vigne Interview, 1961-11-29

ctx.x: He probably would. He used to read music. But I don't know of him arranging anything. But my brother arranged music and wrote music. My brother Sidney, the one who played sax, he wrote music. And you see, I was old enough when he died, got killed to remember those things. I remember seeing him sitting down and arranging music. Yeah. Yeah, he used to sit down and arrange music and write it. Yeah, he was pretty good, my brother Sidney was. But I don't remember too much about my daddy doing that, because you see, he…
